stem: Ojas stirs copper sulphate crystals into a glass of water until the liquid looks evenly blue and no crystals can be seen. Separately, he stirs sawdust into a second glass of water; the sawdust floats and clumps near the top.

parts.text: Which claim correctly decides which sample is a solution?

options.text: The blue copper sulphate mixture is a solution because its components are evenly distributed.
The sawdust mixture is a solution because two substances are present together.
Neither is a solution because you can still see two colours or two materials.
Both are solutions because each glass holds water plus another substance.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A solution is a uniform mixture with components evenly distributed; the sawdust mixture is not uniform.

teacher.key_rationale: A solution is a uniform mixture. The even blue copper sulphate mixture qualifies; sawdust that clumps and floats does not. Being two substances together is not enough.
